Tankless water heatersprovide hot water on demand and typically require minimal control, though the desired out- put temperature can be set. Tank-based water heatersstore hot water and are traditionally set to a single temperature, with potential setback temperatures when hot water needs are low. Modern commercial models, however, can support more advanced controls such as custom time-of-day setpoints, or strategies that priori- tize heating water to the maximum temperature in the configured temperature when electricity prices are low, improving energy efficiency and operational flexibility. • Temperature Controlis managed through thermostats, which regulate heating and cooling setpoints to main- tain occupant comfort and energy efficiency. Smart thermostatsexpand this functionality by supporting custom time-of-day and day-of-week setpoints, allowing for temperature setbacks–automatic adjustments dur- ing unoccupied or low-activity periods to reduce energy without sacrificing comfort when spaces are occupied. In commercial buildings, these thermostats can integrate with building automation systems or operate within a network of zone-level controls to optimize HVAC performance across multiple spaces. When coordinated with occupancy sensors or scheduling software, smart thermostats enable fine-grained control strategies that lower operating costs, reduce peak demand, and contribute to overall building energy management goals. However, they are a big investment, and they can lock in conventional energy production for decades. 2.1.2 Large and Small Appliances With the rise in IoT devices, appliances are not exempt. While many of the features are centered around convenience, they can add safety and increase savings by taking advantage of variable energy pricing. They also allow users to monitor and start devices via apps. One disadvantage is that it can force some building owners into brand loyalty if they want to integrate all their devices into one system. • Smart fridgescan show their contents on a display outside (so users do not have to open the door unneces- sarily), keep track of shopping lists, and send notifications if the fridge door is left open. Even high-efficiency refrigerators without smart features may include audible warnings for doors left open for too long or warnings when the water filter needs to be changed. • Smart stovescan notify the user when the oven is done pre-heating, or when they forgot to turn off the stove. They can also be started or turned off remotely.
